entries.source: WO-0004 builder round 4 (sec-review d1be145, adversary, clean-room tm-qc 2026-09-29)
entries.finding: the offline bundle carries 373 lockstep siblings (520 .debs, 187 MB), among them libc6-dev, python3-dev, slapd and krb5-kdc; install/README.md said "no compiler and no -dev headers"
entries.disposition: round 4 CORRECTED THE CLAIM (measured contents; apt never installs a sibling that is not already installed). entries.source: sec-review TM-SEC-003 (CWE-307), remainder
entries.finding: sign-in rate limiting exists only in nginx (per client address); there is no application-level limiter keyed by identity across the four workers
entries.disposition: the bypass is CLOSED in round 4 (gunicorn listens only on a 0660 topic-manager:www-data Unix socket, so nothing but nginx reaches it); a per-identity limiter is deferred

entries.source: sec-review TM-SEC-011 (CWE-295), first half; brief A11
entries.finding: a TLS upload is not checked against the server name
entries.disposition: DECIDED by the builder, round 4, for owner confirmation: WARN, not refuse. The root helper reads the first server_name of the installed nginx site and, when no SAN covers it (RFC 6125; IP SANs as addresses), the apply result carries "the certificate does not name this server (<name>) ... will refuse it". Refusing would block installing a certificate for a new name before DNS and server_name move, or on a host reached by address

entries.source: prod deploy v1.2.0 on .90, 2026-09-30
entries.finding: The FULL online upgrade (upgrade-full.sh with --repo-url, no --audit-only/--backup-only) does not print the final 'RESULT: exit N' line promised by round 7 (M1); --audit-only and --backup-only do. README/INSTALL tell the operator to read `tail -n 1` of the log, which on the full run shows the Rollback line instead.
entries.where: install/upgrade-full.sh (the full-run exit path after the post-upgrade checklist)
entries.repro: prod .90: /root/tm-upgrade-1.2.0-full.log ends with 'Rollback: sudo bash /root/tm-v1.2.0/install/upgrade-full.sh --restore 20260930-033204', no RESULT line; t47 covers the doc/script agreement but not this exit path.
entries.closes_when: a t47 case runs the full-upgrade exit path and asserts the last line is RESULT: exit 0
entries.root_cause: install/upgrade-full.sh:3252 `trap - EXIT` on the success path disables the handler that prints RESULT; confirmed on tm-qc (both offline upgrades) and prod (online).

entries.source: prod deploy v1.2.0 on .90, 2026-09-30
entries.finding: After the upgrade's OS patch phase restarts sssd, sssd-nss/pam/pam-priv.socket are 'failed': the host's sssd.conf has 'services = nss, pam', so sssd binds those sockets itself and the socket units collide. sssd is active and identity lookups work. Host configuration, not the product; the upgrade could mask or ignore the sssd socket units in its post-check, or document it.

entries.source: clean-room FRESH install of released v1.2.0 on tm-qc (stig-fips), 2026-09-30
entries.finding: install.sh chooses online vs offline by probing pypi.org (install.sh:918) with no flag to force offline; INSTALL §5b / install/README present the bundle as THE offline install without saying so. On a host with internet the bundle is silently ignored. Offline FRESH install therefore never proven (tm-qc turned out NOT air-gapped).
entries.repro: tm-qc stig-fips (has internet): install.sh from the staged bundle logs 'Install mode: ONLINE' and pulls debs/wheels from the internet
entries.closes_when: install.sh --offline forces bundle-only (fails if anything is missing), docs say so, and a fresh install on a host with egress blocked passes
